welcome.title: Welcome to Your Creami Kitchen
paragraphs: This book has 50 recipes written for the Ninja CREAMi NC300IN and the Ninja Blast portable blender, using ingredients you can order on Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, BigBasket or Amazon, or pick up at the kirana. High-protein pints run through the whole book, alongside kulfi-style desi flavours, gelatos and fruit sorbets.

The recipes are split into six sections: Protein Pints: Whey-Powered; Protein Pints: Greek Yogurt, Turbo & Paneer; Desi Ice Creams; Global Classics; Gelato; and Sorbets, Bowls & Shakes. Start with the reference pages that follow. They explain the programs, the sweeteners and the fixes for common texture problems.

Each recipe page shows a program badge (the button to press), a Blast step for blending the base, a 24-hour freeze, the spin and any re-spin. Quantities are metric first, with Indian cups (240 ml) in brackets. Use the notes area to record your freezer's quirks, sweetness changes and the brands you prefer.

how_it_works.text: Add the cold or room-temperature base to the Blast and blend 30–60 s. Cook-and-cool recipes must be fully cool before they go in.
Rest the blended base 2–3 min, or tap the vessel on the counter, so the foam from whey or yogurt subsides.
Pour into a CREAMi pint up to, never above, the MAX FILL line (about 400–450 ml). Lid it and label it with the name and date.
Freeze the pint on a level shelf for a full 24 hours at -13 °C to -22 °C. A slanted pint freezes with an uneven top.
Remove the lid, flatten any hump, lock the pint into the outer bowl and press the program shown on the recipe.
If it looks powdery or crumbly, add 1–2 tbsp milk and press RE-SPIN. Lite and protein bases often need one or two.
Dig a 4 cm well, add up to ⅓ cup mix-ins and run MIX-IN. Flatten leftovers, refreeze, and re-spin before serving again.

programs.name: ICE CREAM
programs.best_for: Full-fat bases with cream, milk and sugar or condensed milk
programs.use_when: The base has real sugar and at least some cream

programs.name: LITE ICE CREAM
programs.texture: Soft-serve once re-spun; may start powdery
programs.use_when: Using whey, Greek yogurt, paneer, stevia, sucralose, erythritol or allulose

programs.name: GELATO
programs.use_when: The base was cooked and cooled: gelato, kulfi, rabdi, caramel

programs.name: SORBET
programs.use_when: Mango, jamun, kokum, lemon or watermelon with sugar or syrup

programs.name: SMOOTHIE BOWL
programs.best_for: Frozen fruit with yogurt, juice or milk
programs.use_when: You want a breakfast bowl to top with granola and fruit

programs.name: MILKSHAKE
programs.best_for: A frozen or processed pint plus about 120 ml milk
programs.use_when: Turning a pint (or leftovers) into a shake in about 2 minutes

programs.name: MIX-IN
programs.best_for: Folding in biscuits, nuts, chocolate or ripples
programs.use_when: The pint is already processed and a 4 cm well is dug to the bottom

programs.name: RE-SPIN
programs.best_for: Rescuing powdery, crumbly or too-cold results
programs.use_when: After any program, with 1–2 tbsp milk added; repeat if needed

blast.intro: The Ninja Blast holds 530 ml with a practical max fill of about 470 ml, so one full pint base blends in a single go. It is cordless and charges by USB-C.
dos: Blend cold or room-temperature bases for 30–60 s, or 2–3 blend cycles.
Add liquids first, then powders (whey, cocoa, gum), then soft solids.
Rest whey and yogurt bases 2–3 min so foam settles before pouring.
Sprinkle xanthan or guar gum over moving liquid to avoid lumps.
Charge it fully before a batch day; one charge covers several pints.
donts: Never blend hot liquids: the sealed vessel builds pressure.
Don't grind hard nuts, ice or whole spices on their own.
Don't knead thick doughs or very dense pastes without liquid.
Don't submerge the motor base in water; rinse only the jar and lid.

golden_rules.title: Freeze a full 24 hours
golden_rules.text: A part-frozen core gives soupy, uneven results. Plan one day ahead.

golden_rules.title: Respect MAX FILL
golden_rules.text: Overfilled pints can jam or damage the machine. Keep bases at about 400–450 ml.

golden_rules.title: Freeze level
golden_rules.text: Set pints on a flat shelf away from the door. A slanted top strains the blade.

golden_rules.title: Flatten the hump
golden_rules.text: If the top freezes domed, rest 5–10 min or scrape it flat with a spoon before spinning.

golden_rules.title: Powdery is normal
golden_rules.text: Lite and protein pints often come out crumbly first. Add 1–2 tbsp milk and re-spin.

golden_rules.title: Never cook whey
golden_rules.text: Heat makes whey grainy and clumpy. Blend it into a cold or cooled base.

golden_rules.title: Keep whey to 1–1.5 scoops
golden_rules.text: 30–45 g per pint is the sweet spot; more turns chalky and icy.

golden_rules.title: Use a pinch of gum
golden_rules.text: ⅛–¼ tsp xanthan or guar gum makes low-fat bases noticeably creamier.

golden_rules.title: Cool before you Blast
golden_rules.text: Cooked bases for gelato, kulfi or chai must reach room temperature before blending.

golden_rules.title: Mix-ins go in last
golden_rules.text: Add them after processing, into a 4 cm well, and use MIX-IN, never the main program.

protein_guide.intro: Protein sources freeze differently. Fat-free and high-protein bases freeze harder, so expect a re-spin and add a pinch of gum. Figures are typical label values; check your pack.

rows.tip: Add gum + 1 tbsp cream or SMP
Thickens on standing; add 2–3 tbsp extra milk
Balance tang with honey or fruit

rows.texture: Very thick, fat-free, firm when frozen
rows.tip: Thin with milk; plan one re-spin
Crumble and blend with milk until fully smooth
Use as the liquid; sweetness is already low

sweetener_guide.name: Sugar
sweetener_guide.tip: Grind to caster so it dissolves in cold bases

sweetener_guide.name: Condensed milk (Milkmaid)
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: Soft and creamy, adds milk solids
sweetener_guide.tip: About 100 g sweetens a pint; whisk in first

sweetener_guide.name: Honey / jaggery
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: Softer than sugar; jaggery adds caramel notes
sweetener_guide.tip: Add jaggery to warm, not boiling, milk to avoid curdling

sweetener_guide.name: Sucralose / aspartame (Sugar Free Natura / Gold)
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: No softening; freezes hard and powdery
sweetener_guide.tip: Add to cold bases (aspartame loses sweetness with heat); plan a re-spin

sweetener_guide.name: Stevia (Sugar Free Green)
sweetener_guide.tip: Use less than you think; vanilla masks the aftertaste

sweetener_guide.name: Erythritol / monk fruit blends
sweetener_guide.tip: Mix with allulose; eat within a week

sweetener_guide.name: Allulose
sweetener_guide.freeze_effect: Softer than sugar, like a regular ice cream
sweetener_guide.tip: Best sugar-free option for scoopable pints

sweetener_guide.name: Dates
sweetener_guide.tip: Soak in hot water 15 min, cool, then Blast with the milk

troubleshooting.why: Low fat or sugar, or a very cold freezer
troubleshooting.fix: Add 1–2 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN; repeat once if needed

troubleshooting.why: Too much water, too little fat, sugar or solids
troubleshooting.fix: Add SMP, cream or a pinch of gum next time

troubleshooting.why: Too much sugar, honey or allulose, or freezer too warm
troubleshooting.fix: Refreeze 1–2 h; reduce sweetener; check freezer is -18 °C

troubleshooting.why: Base expanded as it froze; pint not level
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 5–10 min or scrape flat before spinning

troubleshooting.why: Added without a well, or too many
troubleshooting.fix: Dig a 4 cm well to the bottom; max ⅓ cup; use MIX-IN

troubleshooting.why: Whey or yogurt whipped air into the base
troubleshooting.fix: Rest 2–3 min or tap the Blast before pouring

troubleshooting.why: Too much whey, or isolate with no fat
troubleshooting.fix: Stay at 1–1.5 scoops; add 2 tbsp cream or SMP

troubleshooting.problem: Machine won't start / bowl won't lock
troubleshooting.why: Lid, bowl or pint not seated and twisted fully
troubleshooting.fix: Twist the outer bowl until it clicks; check the paddle is fitted

troubleshooting.why: Pint refroze solid after the first spin
troubleshooting.fix: Flatten the top, add 1 tbsp milk, run the program again

troubleshooting.why: Whey heated, or acidic fruit added to hot milk
troubleshooting.fix: Cool bases first; add fruit and whey cold

storage: Flatten the surface of leftovers with a spoon, lid tightly and refreeze; re-spin before serving again.
Plain dairy pints keep best for 2–3 weeks; protein, sugar-free and sorbet pints for 1–2 weeks.
Refreeze a pint only once or twice; repeated thawing makes it icy.
Label every lid with recipe name, date and program; masking tape and a marker work well.
Keep pints at the back of a level shelf, away from the door, at about -18 °C.
shopping_tips: Keep a standing basket of milk, cream, Milkmaid, cocoa, whey and xanthan, so a pint takes one reorder.
Order cream and Greek yogurt last, check the expiry date on delivery, and refrigerate straight away.
Check marshmallows, sprinkles and jelly sweets for the FSSAI green dot; many imported ones contain gelatin.
Buy specialty items such as xanthan gum, pistachio paste and vanilla extract from Urban Platter on Amazon.
Buy mango pulp tins in May–June when stock is fresh, and freeze seasonal fruit pulp in pint-sized batches.
Compare whey per-scoop protein on the label, not the pack size; flavoured tubs vary widely.
